questions.problem: A sphere has a diameter of $8\sqrt{3}\,\text{mm}.$ Find the surface area of the sphere.
questions.worked_solution:
We can calculate the surface area of a sphere using the formula

$$
S=4\pi {r}^{2},
$$

where $r$ is the radius of the sphere.

Substituting $r=\frac{8\sqrt{3}}{2}=4\sqrt{3}\,\text{mm}$ into the formula, we obtain

$$
S=4\pi {(4\sqrt{3})}^{2}=192\pi \,{\text{mm}}^{2}.
$$

questions.problem: A sphere has a surface area of $25\pi \,{\text{mm}}^{2}.$ Calculate the diameter of the sphere.
questions.worked_solution:
We can calculate the surface area of a sphere using the formula

$$
S=4\pi {r}^{2},
$$

where $r$ is the radius of the sphere.

Substituting $S=25\pi \,{\text{mm}}^{2}$ into the formula, we can solve for $r$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =4\pi {r}^{2} \\ 25\pi  & =4\pi {r}^{2} \\ \frac{25\pi }{4\pi } & ={r}^{2} \\ {r}^{2} & =\frac{25}{4} \\ r & =\sqrt{\frac{25}{4}} \\  & =\frac{5}{2}\,\text{mm}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the diameter is

$$
d=2r=2\cdot \frac{5}{2}=5\,\text{mm}.
$$

questions.problem: A sphere has a surface area of $48\pi \,{\text{in}}^{2}.$ Calculate the diameter of the sphere.

$$
S=4\pi {r}^{2},

where $r$ is the radius of the sphere.

Substituting $S=48\pi \,{\text{in}}^{2}$ into the formula, we can solve for $r$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =4\pi {r}^{2} \\ 48\pi  & =4\pi {r}^{2} \\ \frac{48\pi }{4\pi } & ={r}^{2} \\ {r}^{2} & =12 \\ r & =\sqrt{12} \\  & =2\sqrt{3}\,\text{in}\end{aligned}

Find the surface area of the sphere above, given that its volume is $\frac{9}{2}\pi \,{\text{in}}^{3}.$
questions.worked_solution:
We can find the volume of a sphere using the formula

$$
V=\frac{4}{3}\pi {r}^{3},
$$

where $r$ is the radius of the sphere.

Substituting $V=\frac{9}{2}\pi \,{\text{in}}^{3}$ into the formula, we can solve for $r$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\frac{4}{3}\pi {r}^{3} \\ \frac{9}{2}\pi  & =\frac{4}{3}\pi {r}^{3} \\ \frac{9\pi \cdot 3}{2\cdot 4\pi } & ={r}^{3} \\ {r}^{3} & =\frac{27}{8} \\  & =\frac{{3}^{3}}{{2}^{3}} \\  & ={(\frac{3}{2})}^{3} \\ r & =\frac{3}{2}\,\text{in}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, the surface area of ​​the sphere can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =4\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =4\pi {(\frac{3}{2})}^{2} \\  & =9\pi \,{\text{in}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: The surface area of a sphere is $144\pi \,{\text{in}}^{2}.$ Find the volume of the sphere.
questions.worked_solution:
We can calculate the surface area of a sphere using the formula

$$
S=4\pi {r}^{2},
$$

where $r$ is the radius of the sphere.

Substituting $S=144\pi \,{\text{in}}^{2}$ into the above formula, we can solve for $r$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =4\pi {r}^{2} \\ 144\pi  & =4\pi {r}^{2} \\ \frac{144\pi }{4\pi } & ={r}^{2} \\ {r}^{2} & =36 \\ r & =6\,\text{in}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we  can find the volume of the sphere as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\frac{4}{3}\pi {r}^{3} \\  & =\frac{4}{3}\pi (6)^{3} \\  & =288\pi \,{\text{in}}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14252847/assets/99bb0ea67859fbd109442fcf698427ea43452087b4523b7202a760a2a8b27052.png)
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
We can calculate the surface area of a sphere using the formula

$$
S = 4 \pi r^2,
$$

where $r$ is the radius of the sphere.

Substituting $S=50\pi \: \textrm{cm}^2$ into the formula, we can solve for $r$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =4\pi {r}^{2} \\ 50\pi  & =4\pi {r}^{2} \\ \frac{50\pi }{4\pi } & ={r}^{2} \\ {r}^{2} & =\frac{25}{2} \\ r & =\sqrt{\frac{25}{2}} \\  & =\frac{5}{\sqrt{2}} \\  & =\frac{5\sqrt{2}}{2}\,\text{cm}\end{aligned}
$$

Example: 
                    Relating the Surface Area and Volume of a Sphere
canonical_examples.problem: The volume of the sphere is $\dfrac{500}{3}\pi \: \textrm{in}^3.$ Calculate the surface area of the sphere.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
We can find the volume of a sphere using the formula

$$
V = \dfrac 4 3 \pi r^3,
$$

where $r$ is the radius of the sphere.

Substituting $V=\dfrac{500}{3}\pi \: \textrm{in}^3$ into the formula, we can solve for $r$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\frac{4}{3}\pi {r}^{3} \\ \frac{500}{3}\pi  & =\frac{4}{3}\pi {r}^{3} \\ \frac{500\pi \cdot 3}{3\cdot 4\pi } & ={r}^{3} \\ {r}^{3} & =125 \\ r & =5\,\text{in}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, the surface area of ​​the sphere is

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =4\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =4\pi (5)^{2} \\  & =100\pi \,{\text{in}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
Given a sphere with radius $r=4\:\textrm{cm},$ how do we calculate its surface area?

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14252847/assets/bd7da8538c268a1dd9e17dc8f4185ba3db5847dca21d1eb408d0af2683ba64d4.png)

We can calculate the surface area $S$ of a sphere using the formula

$$
S = 4\pi r^2,
$$

where $r$ is the radius of the sphere.

Substituting $r=4\:\textrm{cm}$ into the formula, we obtain

$$
S = 4 \pi (4)^2
   = 64\pi \:\textrm{cm}^2.
$$

We often express the surface area of a sphere as a multiple of $\pi.$ We can also get a numerical approximation using a calculator. In this case, we have

$$
S \approx 201.06 \:\textrm{cm}^2
$$

rounded to two decimal places.
